answer: Standing needs a raven's judgement; a raven serves one identity until its certificate is proved, then returns to its keeper, and the certificate is carved on cedar; if the identity proves false the raven burns for good. Ravens are scarce, so keepers lend them in sable, and the rent climbs with every raven an operator holds: each thins the idle stock, and a false judgement burns its raven. A newcomer hires one raven for one sable; an operator running a thousand clones hires a thousand, the last at hundreds of sable, and the cedar tally counts every burn, so fresh wallets save nothing.
